newsitem.title: USA: Torchmark says Alabama ruling significant.
newsitem.headline: Torchmark says Alabama ruling significant.

text.p: Torchmark Corp said the Alabama Supreme Court has issued a ruling in a non-Torchmark case that it believes is significant from its perspective.

The court discarded the "justifiable reliance" standard for all fraud cases filed after March 14, 1997 and reinstated the "reasonable reliance" standard to determine whether a fraud was committed and when a fraud claim accrued and the two year statute of limitations commenced, Torchmark said.

The reasonable reliance standard should allow the judge a greater ability to grant summary judgment in appropriate cases based upon all circumstances surrounding a transaction and provide juries with more concrete standards for determining whether a fraud has occurred, Torchmark said.
The Alabama Supreme Court has been asked to reconsider this ruling and this petition is pending, Torchmark said.
"From Torchmark's perspective the new standard has particular significance for cases brought after March 14, 1997 alleging fraud occurring prior to March 14, 1995," the company said.
Torchmark also said the inventory of pending litigation remained relatively constant since last reported.
Dispositions of existing cases balanced new lawsuits, the company said.

The number of lawsuits filed in 1997 declined substantially when comparing 1997 and 1996. Other litigation events have been separately reported in filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the company said.
